info.title: WaAPI API
info.description:
WaAPI is a simple API gateway for sending messages.

## Response envelopes

Every `/instances/{id}/client/action/*` call answers with two status fields:

| Field | Answers |
|---|---|
| `status` | Did the request reach the instance? |
| `data.status` | Did the instance carry the action out? **This is the authoritative one.** |

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "links": { "self": "https://waapi.app/api/v1/instances/123/client/action/send-message" },
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "instanceId": "123",
    "data": { }
  }
}
```

A malformed input is **not** an HTTP error. It comes back as HTTP 200 with
`status: success` and `data.status: error`, and nothing was sent:

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { "status": "error", "message": "incorrect chatId format.", "explanation": "…" }
}
```

Check `data.status` before treating any action as done.

## Chat and contact IDs

| Form | Addresses |
|---|---|
| `<number>@c.us` | a contact by phone number — country code and number, digits only (`491729682587@c.us`) |
| `<lid>@lid` | the same contact by its Linked ID (LID), an identifier that does not reveal the phone number |
| `<id>@g.us` | a group |
| `<id>@newsletter` | a channel |

Incoming messages and events can carry a contact's `@lid` form in `from`, `author` and participant lists —
also for contacts you know by phone number. Both forms address the same one-to-one chat: replying to the
`from` you received reaches that person, whether it ends in `@c.us` or `@lid`. To map one form to the
other, call `get-lid`; it resolves in both directions. Every `chatId`, `contactId` and `participant`
parameter accepts the `@lid` form.

post.summary: send a text message to a chat
post.description:
Send a text message to a chat. The chatId format varies depending on the chat type:
- Individual chat: {phone_number}@c.us (e.g. 50664083362@c.us)
- Group chat: {group_id}@g.us (e.g. 123456789-123456789@g.us)
- Channel/Newsletter: {channel_id}@newsletter (e.g. 123456789@newsletter)

chatId.description: Chat ID: `<number>@c.us` or `<lid>@lid` for a contact (both address the same chat), `<id>@g.us` for a group.

message.description: Text message to send. Can include @123456789 for group chats.

mentions.description: Optional array of contact IDs to mention. Only works in group chats. Make sure to include @123456789 in the message text.

replyToMessageId.description: Optional message ID to reply to. Format: {fromMe}_{chatId}_{messageId}

previewLink.description: Whether to show link previews in the message. Defaults to true.

firedandforget.description: Set to true to process the request asynchronously. Returns a reference UUID for polling via GET /instances/{id}/request/{reference}. Alias: faf

200.description: Request reached the instance. `data.status` reports whether the action was carried out; on error `data` carries `message` and `explanation`. Payload: Message sent successfully.

data.description: The action's outcome. `status: success` carries the payload; `status: error` is an `actionError`.

403.description: Forbidden — insufficient permissions or account blocked

404.description: Not found — instance does not exist or does not belong to you

422.description: Validation error — invalid or missing request parameters, or the send was refused before it was attempted. A send is refused when the recipient's number is not registered (override with `skipNumberCheck: true`), or when the connected account is under a reach-out restriction and this exact recipient has already been observed being rejected — contacts who replied are unaffected, and retrying counts towards the limit that caused the restriction. The `message` field names which of the two applies.

post.summary: send a media message (image, video, audio, document)
post.description:
Send a media file to a chat. Provide either `mediaUrl` (a publicly accessible URL) or `mediaBase64` (base64-encoded file content with `mediaName`), but not both.

The chatId format varies depending on the chat type:
- Individual chat: {phone_number}@c.us (e.g. 123456789@c.us)
- Group chat: {group_id}@g.us (e.g. 123456789-123456789@g.us)
- Channel/Newsletter: {channel_id}@newsletter (e.g. 123456789@newsletter)

Supported media types:
- Images: jpg, jpeg, png, gif
- Videos: mp4, 3gp, mov
- Audio: mp3, wav, ogg, m4a
- Documents: pdf, doc, docx, txt, xlsx, etc

post.summary: [BETA] subscribe to and fetch current presence of a chat
post.description:
Subscribes to presence updates for the given chat and returns the current state. Subsequent changes emit presence_update webhook events (if enabled in webhook settings).

**Important — subscription model:**
- Presence in Web is subscription-based. You MUST call this action at least once per chat you want to track. Without a subscribe, the presence_update webhook never fires for that chat.
- Calling this action again acts as a renewal. Subscriptions are lost on instance reconnect — re-subscribe after any 'ready' event if you want continuous tracking.
- Privacy reciprocity: if the instance account hides its own last-seen in the settings, it cannot read others' last-seen either. Expect deny:true or hasData:false in that case.
- High-frequency event — a single active chat can produce 10+ presence_update webhooks per minute. Debounce on your side.
- Groups: chatstate is always null. Use typingParticipants and recordingParticipants instead. isOnline on a group = 'at least one member online'.

Note: This endpoint is currently in beta and may change without notice.

call_policy.description: On create, omitting it means no policy (ignore); on update, omitting it leaves the stored policy unchanged. `null` resets to ignore in both.

instanceUpdate.description: Send protection is managed on the instance page in your account, not through the API.

data.description: Reserved. `null` in every observed response.

instanceCallPolicy.description: The call policy the instance runs with. Returned by `PUT /instances/{id}` only — `GET /instances/{id}/client/status` never carries it. Note the shape: camelCase (`audioUrl`, `videoUrl`, `hangupAfterSeconds`), not the snake_case one requests use.

nodeReachable.description: Returned by `PUT /instances/{id}` only, and only as `false`: the update was stored but the running instance could not be reached to be told about it, so it keeps its previous settings until it reconnects. Absent whenever no such failure happened — including on every `GET /instances/{id}/client/status`, which never carries this field.

callPolicy.description: How the instance handles incoming calls. `null` or mode `ignore` means the call webhook fires and nothing else. Two requirements the schema cannot express: reject_with_message requires message, and answer_and_play requires audio_url or video_url — without them the request is answered with a 422.

message.example: We do not take calls. Please send a message.
message.description: Text sent to the caller after rejecting (mode reject_with_message)

audio_url.description: wav, mp3 or ogg played into the call (mode answer_and_play), max 25 MB

video_url.description: mp4 (H.264) looped as the camera on video calls (mode answer_and_play), max 25 MB

hangup_after_seconds.description: Hang up at the latest this many seconds after the call connected (mode answer_and_play)

callPolicyNodeShape.description: The call policy as the instance itself runs it: the same policy as `callPolicy`, with camelCase keys. `{ "mode": "ignore" }` alone when no policy is stored; otherwise every key is present and the unused ones are `null`. Read-only — requests always use the snake_case `callPolicy`.

message.example: We do not take calls. Please send a message.
message.description: Text sent to the caller after rejecting (mode reject_with_message)

audioUrl.description: wav, mp3 or ogg played into the call (mode answer_and_play), max 25 MB

videoUrl.description: mp4 (H.264) looped as the camera on video calls (mode answer_and_play), max 25 MB

hangupAfterSeconds.description: Hang up at the latest this many seconds after the call connected (mode answer_and_play)

callState.description: The call's state, as the platform's own CallState enum — all fifteen members: 0 None, 1 Calling, 2 PreacceptReceived, 3 ReceivedCall (an incoming call is ringing), 4 AcceptSent, 5 AcceptReceived, 6 CallActive (connected), 7 CallActiveElseWhere (answered on another linked device), 8 ReceivedCallWithoutOffer, 9 Rejoining, 10 Link, 11 ConnectedLonely, 12 PreCalling (an outgoing call that is not registered yet), 13 CallStateEnding, 14 CallBCallStarting. In practice you will see 3, 6, 12 and 13; start-call with waitForAnswer false can report 12, and 7 reaches the call webhook. Treat any other value as one of the states above rather than as an error.

from.description: The peer — the caller for an incoming call, the callee for an outgoing one

fromMe.description: true for calls placed by this instance

timedOut.description: start-call only: answerTimeout elapsed and the call was hung up

eventType.description: A webhook event. `call` fires when a call comes in or is placed. Its `data.call` is the raw call object — every field of the `call` schema (including `state`) plus `canHandleLocally`, `webClientShouldHandle` and `participants`; the action responses carry the `call` schema itself, and nothing more. The instance's `call_policy` is applied after the event went out. `call_ended` fires once the call is over, with `data` as `{ peer, outcome (Completed, Missed, Rejected, Canceled, AcceptedElsewhere, Failed or Unknown), duration (seconds), isVideo, fromMe, timestamp, messageId }`.

chatId.description: Chat ID <countrycode_short><usernumber>@c.us or @g.us for groups

chatPresence.description: Presence state of a chat. Returned by get-chat-presence action and included in presence_update webhook events. Null fields carry semantic meaning — read the field descriptions before interpreting them.

id.description: Serialized chat id this presence refers to.

isGroup.description: Whether this presence refers to a group chat.

isOnline.description: Whether the contact (or any group member) is currently online. For groups this is an aggregate across all members.

chatstate.description: Current typing/recording state. Null for group chats — use typingParticipants and recordingParticipants instead. The service auto-reverts typing/recording to available/unavailable after ~25 seconds of inactivity, which produces a second presence_update event.

lastSeen.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the contact was last seen. Only populated when chatstate is 'unavailable' AND deny is false. Null in all other cases — do not interpret null as 'never seen'.

deny.description: True when the peer has explicitly blocked last-seen visibility for this account. Typing/online state may still be visible — deny only affects lastSeen.

typingParticipants.description: Group chats only. Serialized JIDs of members currently typing. Empty for 1:1 chats.

recordingParticipants.description: Group chats only. Serialized JIDs of members currently recording audio. Empty for 1:1 chats.

hasData.description: False means subscription is active but the service has not yet pushed any state. Do NOT interpret hasData:false as 'offline' — it means 'unknown'.

isSubscribed.description: Whether this chat is currently subscribed to presence updates.

webhookSubscription.description: A single webhook subscription registered on an instance (as created by Zapier, Make, n8n or a direct API client). Distinct from the instance's own webhook_url/webhook_events, which are set by hand and never expire.

url.description: The URL that will receive event payloads.

source.description: Who is registering this subscription. Defaults to api.

requestStatus.description: Whether the request reached the instance. `success` here does **not** mean the action was carried out — that is reported by `data.status`, which is the authoritative one. A malformed input arrives as `status: success` with `data.status: error`.

actionStatus.description: Whether the instance carried the action out — the authoritative field. In this branch it is always `success`; when the instance refused the action the whole `data` object is an `actionError` with `status: error`, `message` and `explanation`.

actionError.description: Shape of `data` when the instance refused the action. HTTP status is still 200 and the outer `status` is still `success`.

sendProtection.description: Send protection of this instance. Read-only: the switch is on the instance page in your account. While enabled, the instance sends one message at a time with a short pause, and conversations with recipients who have never written to this account are limited per hour and per day. A send over a limit is answered with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header; nothing is sent. A fire-and-forget send is accepted with 202 and a refusal is read from GET /instances/{id}/request/{reference}.

disableable.description: false on trial instances, where the protection is always on.

reason.description: send_paced: too many sends were waiting for this instance. new_conversation_budget: the hourly or daily limit for new conversations is reached.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the send can be retried. Also sent as the Retry-After header.

message.example: Send protection: the limit for new conversations is reached. Retry after the given number of seconds.

settings.description: The instance page where the protection can be reviewed.

sendProtectionRefused.description: Refused by the instance's send protection. Nothing was sent; retry after the given number of seconds. Integrations that already handle 429 need no change.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the send can be retried.
